newsitem.title: USA: NYS lawmakers okay lulus but challenge seen--paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS lawmakers okay lulus but challenge seen--paper.

text.p: New York State lawmakers approved a controversial measure restoring $62,500 of stipends for a handful of Assembly members, but the bill might be challenged in court, the Albany Times Union said Wednesday.

Robert Schulz, a Washington County resident, who has sued the state numerous times for its spending practices, vowed to do so again if Gov George Pataki signs the stipend bill, which was approved, as expected, on Tuesday.

The stipends expired in November, when the governor and Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno (R-Troy), were upset with the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan), for refusing to approve other measures, the paper said.
But the three leaders agreed to settle their differences on some of the matters last weekend, clearing the way for the stipend bill to be approved.

While the state constituion bars sitting lawmakers from increasing their own salaries, a spokeswoman for Silver said the Assembly was confident its pposition would be upheld if it were challenged, as it only restored and did not increase stipends, the Times Union said.
